text:
Washington took a 5-2 win in Raleigh that Carolina probably deserved to lose by less than that, and the first period explains almost all of it. The Capitals scored three times before the game was 15 minutes old, two of them from Alex Tuch, on a combined 2.17 expected goals to Carolina's 0.71. Tuch's backhand at 14:23 was the best of them, a chance worth 54 percent. Jakob Chychrun then made it 4-0 on a power-play snap shot early in the second, off a chance that rated only 3 percent.

After that, the game turned. Carolina outchanced Washington 2.40 to 0.58 in the second period and finished with 81 shot attempts to the Capitals' 43. Over a full game of simulated replays of every shot, the Hurricanes win 64 percent of the time. Sebastian Aho pulled one back on the power play at 16:50, but Ryan Leonard answered eight seconds later, which took the air out of any comeback. Logan Stankoven added a tip-in in the third, and that was all Carolina got.

The difference was in the crease. Logan Thompson faced 33 shots and stopped about two more than the chances predicted, while Brandon Bussi allowed five goals on roughly three goals' worth of shots, nearly two worse than expected. Washington also blocked 28 shots to Carolina's 9, and Andrei Svechnikov put six on net with little to show for it. The Capitals were outplayed for two periods and still won by three, because they cashed in early and their goalie was better.
